fields.v: Gao, H., Baltes, S., Lulla, J. L., Treude, C., Lin, H. Y., Zahedi, M. (2026). From Registry to Repository: How AI Agent Skills Are Written, Adapted, and Maintained. arXiv:2607.00911v2 [cs.SE], 6 Jul 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2607.00911v2 [cs.SE]; no published venue stated
The University of Melbourne (Gao, Lin, Zahedi); Heidelberg University (Baltes); Singapore Management University (Lulla, Treude)

Evaluates; secondary: Compares — empirical mining study of AI agent skills as software artefacts (SWEBOK classification, packaging and spec conformance, content taxonomy, customisation and evolution), comparing registry vs personal-use skills and customisation vs evolution; no agent configuration run
fields.why: The study evaluates no SDD approach or agent configuration; it characterises skill artefacts by mining. 'Evaluates; secondary: Compares' is the closest fit in the closed list, but the main nature is a judgement call (no value fits an artefact-mining study well).

fields.v: Agent Skills (SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter + Markdown body + optional scripts/, references/, assets/), per the public Agent Skills specification supported by Anthropic (agentskills.io; version Not stated, accessed 28-06-2026); skills from the skills.sh registry and personal-use GitHub repositories

SKILL.md (frontmatter: name, description mandatory; license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools optional); optional scripts/, references/, assets/ directories; spec recommends body <= 500 lines, <= 5,000 whitespace tokens, relative Markdown links at most one directory deep. Content taxonomy found: scoping/orchestrating, execution lifecycle, output quality, governing agent conduct, domain knowledge, user/agent coordination
Not applicable to skills as a whole (skills loaded on demand by progressive disclosure: frontmatter preloaded, body on activation); 68% of sampled skills prescribe a sequenced/branching workflow
Not stated as a prescribed flow; 63% of sampled skills contain user-interaction rules (e.g., gating consequential actions behind user consent)
Not run, document-based (mining of SKILL.md files and their git histories)
Not classifiable (skills are reusable context bundles, not specifications; authors call workflow parts 'operational specifications')
N/A (mining study); skills come from existing open-source repositories and a registry

18,463 registry skills (skills.sh, >= 20 installs, 2,338 repos) + 23,199 personal-use skills (5,876 GitHub repos); 3,709 reuse links (2,462 SE pairs); 29,450 SE skills after classification; 180 skills thematically analysed; 444 diffs coded (188 linked, 256 unlinked)
Agent skills across SWEBOK knowledge areas (Software Construction dominant: 28.3% registry, 22.1% personal) plus ~29% non-SE skills

Conformance to 17 statically checkable provisions of the Agent Skills specification (7 mandatory, 10 optional); length and header structure
None (maintenance activity measured as commits: 58.8% of all 16,244 SE personal-use skills updated at least once; locally authored 60.8%, median 2 follow-up commits; reused 47.4%)

SWEBOK KA distribution; reuse linkage and verbatim-copy rate (70.3% pairs similarity >= 0.99); upstream synchronisation (40.2% of never-updated reused skills missed upstream updates; 62.3% diverged); taxonomies of content (6 themes, 17 subthemes, 69 codes) and changes (6 themes, 60 codes); addition/removal ratio

Automatic mining (skills.sh, GitHub Search API, commit histories, LCS similarity); LLM classification (Qwen3.6-27b, temperature 0, validated against a 285-skill gold standard, kappa 0.82); manual thematic analysis and open coding by two authors; Mann-Whitney U, Cliff's delta, Fisher's exact with Benjamini-Hochberg, Cohen's h
N/A (document-based mining study; no configuration run)

Document-based: centralised (registry) vs personal-use skills on KA distribution, structure and specification conformance; customisation (registry-to-local adoption diff, 188 linked pairs) vs evolution (initial-to-final diff of locally authored skills, 256), stratified by similarity/churn quartiles. No agent, acceptance tests, repetitions or human intervention apply

Registry skills longer (median 1,678 vs 1,114 tokens; 19 vs 13 headers; p < 0.001, Cliff's delta 0.23/0.25) and more spec-conformant (name equals directory 97.65% vs 91.23%); optional fields in 3-16%. Reuse mostly one-time copy: 1,841/2,462 near-verbatim; 47.4% of reused skills locally updated vs 60.8% of local ones; 53% never updated after adoption. Most edited: reworking operational specifications (56.9% customisation / 61.6% evolution) and adapting knowledge (46.3% / 50.2%). Significant differences: repackaging/porting only in customisation (12.2% vs 0%, h = 0.71), renames/tool substitutions in evolution (5.3% vs 24.3%, h = 0.57), polishing presentation in customisation (55.9% vs 30.6%, h = 0.52). Additions outnumber removals 2.7:1 (evolution 6.1:1). User interaction, monitoring and failure-handling rules rarely edited

Distinguished registry vs personal and customisation vs evolution with statistical tests and effect sizes. Linkage heuristic validated (90% agreement, 93% genuine reuse in boundary bucket; 30/30 below threshold independent). Limitations stated: tests ignore clustering within repositories and dependence among labels; endpoint diff hides intermediate edits; exploratory

Single primary KA per skill; linkage misses renamed/heavily edited skills and assumes direction registry -> repo; customisation and evolution use different diff designs; 20-install threshold; LLM labels; gold standard stratified by predicted label; only public GitHub repos; Tukey cap may drop genuine projects; snapshot to March/May 2026; single registry. Gaps: consolidate re-authored domain knowledge, skill activation tracing, prose vs script trade-off, agent-neutral formats and templates

Replication package: zenodo.org/records/21032973. No pre-registration. No programming language (Markdown/YAML artefacts). Not an evaluation of agent performance; relevance to SDD: skills as reusable instruction artefacts. Tables I-III extracted with jumbled columns; values rebuilt by order and checked against text (e.g., h values 0.71 in table vs 0.72 in text for repackaging, p. 8-9). Evolution frame: 5,978 changed skills reduced to 5,367 after churn filter

fields.why: Q3 targets agent runs; no agent is run. The classifier models are named (Qwen3.6-27b, Gemma-4-31b-it, temperature 0, p. 4) and the Agent Skills spec is cited only by URL and access date (p. 12). Partly or Yes are both defensible.

fields.v: Yes (1): data sources, dates and filters described; dataset in replication package

Partly (0.5): LLM labels validated against a two-annotator gold standard (kappa 0.85; classifier kappa 0.82) and linkage audited by two authors, but the gold standard and all thematic codes are the authors' own annotations
fields.why: The gold standard (kappa 0.85 between two annotators), the linkage audit and the thematic codes are all authored by the study's own authors (p. 4-5); the classifier is checked against that gold standard (kappa 0.82). Whether author-built ground truth with inter-rater agreement counts as independent is a judgement: Partly or Yes.
